title: Structure and biochemistry reveal substrate-modulated ComEC nuclease activity during DNA processing.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the full Europe PMC supplement (27.5 MB): it contains only figure images, two movies (MovieS1/S2.mp4), a movie-legend Word file and one 16 MB supplementary PDF. No spreadsheet, CSV or any tabular file exists. Queried the RCSB Protein Data Bank entry records for all three deposited structures and confirmed they are single cryo-electron microscopy models of ComEC from the bacterium Neomoorella carbonis at 4.1-4.2 Angstrom resolution. Scanned the complete open-access full text for supplementary table titles and for any quantification or source-data statement.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The contents of Supplementary Tables S1-S4 (cryo-electron microscopy collection and refinement statistics; bacterial strains; plasmids; primers) were read from the full text, not opened, because the supplementary PDF had no extractable text layer with the tools available. The nuclease assay quantification ('quantified and normalized to t = 0 min, fraction of remaining substrate plotted over time', 'biological replicates') is described in the methods only; the numbers themselves appear only inside figure panels.

a1_downloadable.note: Three Protein Data Bank entries (30BU, 30BT, 32KS) and two Electron Microscopy Data Bank maps (EMD-57548, EMD-57549) are public and I retrieved the PDB entry metadata; the supplement downloaded and unzipped without login.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FIRST KILLER. There is no prediction-target column anywhere. The only quantitative measurements (DNA degradation time courses, position-dependent cleavage, effect of the DNA-binding protein ComEA) exist solely as gel images and plotted curves inside figure panels; a label would have to be reconstructed by reading numbers off figures or re-doing densitometry on published images.

a3_inputs_present.note: Protein sequences and atomic coordinates are retrievable from PDB/UniProt, and the DNA substrate sequences are in the methods, so inputs would be obtainable - but there is nothing to pair them with.

a4_units_stated.note: No units column exists because no data table exists; assay readouts are 'fraction of remaining substrate' described in prose only.

a5_enough_rows.note: Three deposited structures and two maps. The biochemistry is a handful of gel-based assays with a few biological replicates each - orders of magnitude below the ~1,500-row (or ~400 for classification) bar.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Coordinates are tiny; the two cryo-electron microscopy maps are the only sizeable files. Size is not the problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Deposited structures match what the paper and data availability statement describe; nothing to disagree about since there is no table.

a8_label_provenance.note: The only machine-readable 'predictions' in the paper are AlphaFold3 models of the ComEC-DNA translocation complex, i.e. another model's output - using those as labels would be distillation, exactly the circularity A8 forbids.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) would be the natural fit for ComEC sequences
backbone.hardware: CPU would suffice, but there are no labels to fit a head to

integration.partner_dataset: UniProt / AlphaFold Database for ComEC homologues across bacteria
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Could not be written usefully: joining three structures to UniProt adds annotation but no measured outcome to predict.

controls.positive_control: None available - no measured quantity is distributed in machine-readable form.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is undefined without labels.
controls.external_validation: No second dataset of ComEC nuclease activity exists that I could find in the paper or its references.

honest_claim_h3: No honest claim is possible: with three cryo-electron microscopy structures and a handful of gel assays, any model would be fitting noise, so the only defensible statement is that this paper supplies structural evidence, not training data.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein and DNA sequence to predict where a bacterial DNA-uptake enzyme cuts its substrate.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would show the model a ComEC protein sequence (the membrane machine that pulls DNA into bacteria) plus a DNA substrate sequence. Verified count of usable examples: 3 deposited structures and a handful of gel assays, far too few.
plain_idea.predict: Where along the DNA the enzyme cuts, and how fast it degrades the strand. The true answer comes from gel-based nuclease assays read by band densitometry - published only as figure panels, not as numbers.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Natural transformation spreads antibiotic resistance, so understanding how ComEC chooses cut sites matters to microbiologists - but this paper does not provide enough measurements to learn it.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predict ComEC cleavage position and degradation rate from protein plus DNA substrate sequence, or predict channel conformational state from sequence. Both die because the paper's measurements live in gel images and plots, never in a table, and total only a few experiments.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the actual file sizes I unzipped (27.5 MB supplement, tiny PDB coordinate files); nothing was timed because there is no dataset to process.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the rows of machine-readable measurements in the supplement - I did this and the answer is zero: the archive holds only figures, two movies and a PDF.

verdict_reason: A structural biology paper with no dataset: three cryo-electron microscopy structures plus gel assays whose numbers exist only inside figure panels. Fails A2 (no label column), A4 (no units table), A5 (3 structures, a handful of assays) and A8 (the only computed values are AlphaFold3 predictions).
